newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S., Japan said to show flexibility in air talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan said to show flexibility in air talks.

text.p: U.S. Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater and Japanese Transport Minister Makoto Koga signalled flexibility in talks on Monday to dicuss a longstanding dispute over aviation services, a U.S. government official said.
"Both sides presented their positions in ways that led to greater understanding," said the official, who declined to be identified. "Both sides...indicated what flexibilities they have."
"They are genuinely committed on both sides to trying to solve the aviation issues. Both sides are sincere and both sides indicated flexibility."
The officials held the bilateral talks on the margins of an Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum meeting of transportation ministers.

The United States has been seeking an "open skies" agreement to eliminate government restrictions on aviation service. Japan has resisted that effort and instead has proposed allowing two carriers from each country broad access to the other market, an idea the United States has rejected.

During the bilateral talks here, Slater presented proposals on how to achieve full liberalization in ways "acceptable to both countries" including elements the U.S. government feels would be necessary during a transition period, the U.S. official said. He declined to be specific.
Talks are to continue at the assistant-secretary level on July 8 and 9 and at those meetings the U.S. negotiators hope to see movement in the Japanese position, the U.S. official said.
Japanese officials were not available for comment.
